questions.question: Weight of 6 boys P, Q, R, S, T and V is compared. Weight of no two boys is same. Number of boys having weight more than P are same as number of boys having weight less than T. Weight of R is more than only V and T. Weight P is less than only S. Weight of Q is more than how many boys?
questions.solution:
Given that there are **6 boys** P, Q, R, S, T and V with different weights.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. R is heavier than only V and T.

→ The order from heavier to lighter is: **_ > _ > _ > R > T > V**

2. P is lighter than only S.

→ So, P is the **2nd heaviest** and S is the **heaviest**.

→ **S > P > _ > R > T > V**

3. Number of boys heavier than P = Number of boys lighter than T.

→ Boys heavier than P = **1 (only S)**.

→ Therefore, boys lighter than T must also be **1**.

Since only V is lighter than T, this condition is satisfied.

4. The only remaining vacant position is occupied by Q.

→ Final order from heaviest to lightest:

→ **S > P > Q > R > T > V**

Thus, Q is heavier than **R, T and V**, i.e., **3 boys**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 8 AM and 9 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 75 degrees?
questions.solution:
The given time interval is between **8 AM** and **9 AM**.

At **8:00 AM**, the **hour hand** is at 8 × 300 = 2400 and the **minute hand** is at 00.

To find the time when the angle is **75 degrees**, we consider the relative speed = 6 − 0.5 = 5.50 per minute.

**Case 1:** The **minute hand** is behind the **hour hand**.

Relative angular distance to be covered = 240 − 75 = 1650

Time = 165 / 5.5 = 30 minutes. (This corresponds to **8:30 AM**)

**Case 2:** The **minute hand** has crossed the **hour hand**.

Relative angular distance to be covered = 240 + 75 = 3150

Time = 315 / 5.5 = 630 / 11 ≈ **57.27 minutes**.

This corresponds approximately to **8:57 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 3**”. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M|over2

Where **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

Given **Angle = 75** and **H = 8**.

75 = |60 times 8 - 11M|over2

150 = |480 − 11M|

480 − 11M = −150 (since we are looking for the time closer to 9 AM based on options)

11M = 480 + 150

11M = 630

M = 630/11 ≈ 57.27

Therefore, the time is approximately **8:57 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is **8:57**.

questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 10 AM. The clock gains 3 seconds every 4 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 10 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
The time interval from **10 AM** to **10 PM** on the same day is exactly **12 hours**.

Total time in minutes = 12 × 60 = **720 minutes**.

Given that the clock gains **3 seconds every 4 minutes**.

Gain in 1 minute = 3/4 seconds.

Total gain in 720 minutes = 720 × (3/4) seconds

Total gain = 180 × 3 = **540 seconds**.

Now, convert the total gain from seconds into minutes:

Gain in minutes = 540 ÷ 60 = **9 minutes**.

The correct time is 10 PM. Since the clock is gaining time, it will show the correct time plus the gained time.

Time shown by the clock = 10 PM + 9 minutes = **10:09 PM**.

Therefore, the time the clock will show is **10:09:00**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: The 73rd constitutional amendment deals with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panchayati Raj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992** was enacted to institutionalize **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**, providing them with constitutional status and protection.
 
• This amendment inserted a new **Part IX** into the Constitution of India, titled **The Panchayats**, which encompasses provisions from **Article 243 to 243-O**.
 
• It also introduced the **11th Schedule**, which details **29 functional items** or subjects, such as **agriculture**, **land improvement**, and **minor irrigation**, that fall under the jurisdiction of Panchayats.
 
• The act gave practical shape to **Article 40** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, which directs the State to organize village panchayats as units of **self-government**.
 
• It mandates a **three-tier system** of Panchayati Raj in every state: **Gram Panchayat** (village level), **Panchayat Samiti** (intermediate level), and **Zila Parishad** (district level).
 
• The act provides for mandatory **reservation of seats** for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in proportion to their population, and at least **one-third reservation** for **women**.
 
• To ensure financial and electoral autonomy, the act established the **State Finance Commission** to review financial positions and the **State Election Commission** to conduct fair elections every **five years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-defection**:

 
 
• Introduced by the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985** to prevent political defections.
 
• It added the **10th Schedule**, which lays down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection.
 
 
 
• **Tribunals**:
 
 
• Constitutional status was provided by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• It added **Part XIV-A**, containing **Article 323A** for administrative tribunals and **Article 323B** for other matters.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Societies**:
 
 
• Given constitutional status through the **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**.
 
• It added **Part IX-B** and included the right to form cooperatives as a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 19(1)(c)**.

questions.question: The first woman governor of an Indian state was:

The correct answer is __**Sarojini Naidu**__.

• She held this prestigious constitutional office until her death on **March 2, 1949**, making her the **first woman** to serve as a **Governor** in the history of independent India.
 
• Commonly known as the **Nightingale of India** (Bharat Kokila), she was a prolific **poet** and a major political figure in the **Indian National Movement**.
 
• In **1925**, she became the **first Indian woman** to be elected as the **President of the Indian National Congress** during its **Kanpur Session**.
 
• She was a close associate of **Mahatma Gandhi** and played a significant role during the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, including the **Dandi March** and the **Dharasana Satyagraha**.

• **Indira Gandhi**:

 
 
• She was the **first woman Prime Minister of India**, serving from **1966 to 1977** and again from **1980 until 1984**.
 
• She was the first woman to be honored with the **Bharat Ratna** in **1971** for her leadership during the **Indo-Pakistani War**.
 
 
 
• **Sucheta Kripalani**:
 
 
• She became the **first woman Chief Minister** of an Indian state, leading the government of **Uttar Pradesh** from **1963 to 1967**.
 
• She was a member of the **Constituent Assembly** and founded the **All India Mahila Congress** in **1940**.
 
 
 
• **Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit**:

questions.question: How many pollutants are measured under India's Air Quality Index (AQI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Air Quality Index (AQI)** was launched in **September 2014** in New Delhi under the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** to provide a simplified health-related air quality status to the public.
 
• Developed by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in consultation with **IIT Kanpur** and medical professionals, it follows the mantra of **One Number-One Colour-One Description**.
 
• The index measures **eight major pollutants** for which short-term national standards have been prescribed. These are **Particulate Matter (PM10)**, **Particulate Matter (PM2.5)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)**, **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Ozone (O₃)**, **Ammonia (NH₃)**, and **Lead (Pb)**.
 
• The **AQI** calculation is based on the **24-hour average** concentration for most pollutants, except for **Ozone** and **Carbon Monoxide**, which are monitored on an **8-hour average** basis to better reflect immediate health impacts.
 
• The overall AQI for a location is determined by the **sub-index** of the pollutant that is most prominent (the pollutant with the highest concentration relative to its standard) on a given day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AQI Categories and Health Impact**:

 
 
• **Good (0−50)**: Minimal health impact.
 
• **Satisfactory (51−100)**: May cause minor breathing discomfort to sensitive individuals.
 
• **Moderately Polluted (101−200)**: May cause breathing discomfort to people with asthma and heart diseases.
 
• **Poor (201−300)**: Causes breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure.
 
• **Very Poor (301−400)**: Leads to respiratory illness upon prolonged exposure.
 
• **Severe (401−500)**: Affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing respiratory or cardiovascular ailments.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with NAAQS**:
 
 
• While the AQI monitors **8 pollutants**, the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** officially monitor **12 pollutants**.
 
• The four pollutants included in NAAQS but excluded from daily AQI reporting are **Benzene**, **Benzo(a)pyrene**, **Arsenic**, and **Nickel**, as they are primarily monitored for long-term (annual) chronic exposure rather than short-term spikes.

questions.question: Freedom to make life choices in the Happiness Index refers to:

options.text: People's perception of having control over life decisions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People's perception of having control over life decisions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report** utilizes six key variables to explain the variation in happiness across different nations, one of which is the **Freedom to make life choices**.
 
• This specific metric is defined as the national average of binary responses (0 or 1) to the **Gallup World Poll** question: 'Are you satisfied or dissatisfied with your freedom to choose what you do with your life?'.
 
• It represents an individual's **subjective perception** of their own **autonomy** and the extent to which they feel they have the agency to steer their own life path without undue restriction.
 
• Unlike objective measures of **civil liberties** or **legal rights**, this indicator focuses on the internal psychological state of feeling 'free', which is highly correlated with overall **life satisfaction**.
 
• Data collected indicates that a strong sense of personal agency is a fundamental pillar of human well-being, often ranking as more significant than absolute income in developed economies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Happiness Index** is published annually by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**.
 
• The index is calculated using a three-year average of data, primarily employing the **Cantril Ladder**, where respondents rate their lives on a scale from 0 to 10.
 
• Other core variables in the report include:
 
 
• **GDP per Capita**: A measure of the average **economic output** per person, adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**.
 
• **Social Support**: Evaluated by asking if citizens have relatives or friends they can count on during trouble.
 
• **Healthy Life Expectancy**: Extracted from **World Health Organization (WHO)** data, reflecting physical health and longevity.
 
• **Generosity**: Calculated based on the residual of average responses to questions regarding donating money to charity.
 
• **Perceptions of Corruption**: Measured by the perceived level of corruption in government and business sectors.

questions.question: Which state hosted the 37th National Games of India in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **37th edition** of the **National Games of India** was officially held in the state of **Goa** from **October 26 to November 9, 2023**.
 
• This was the **first time** that Goa hosted the prestigious multi-sport event, which saw participation from over **10,000 athletes** representing all **28 states**, **8 Union Territories**, and the **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)**.
 
• The games were inaugurated by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** at the **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** located in **Fatorda**, South Goa.
 
• The official **mascot** for the event was named **Moga**, an **Indian Bison (Gaur)**, which is the state animal of Goa; the name **Moga** is derived from the **Konkani** word for love or affection.
 
• The competition featured a record **43 sporting disciplines**, including the debut of sports such as **Beach Football**, **Rollball**, **Golf**, **Sepaktakraw**, **Kalaripayattu**, **Lagori**, and **Pencak Silat**.
 
• The events were organized across five main Goan cities: **Panaji**, **Margao**, **Mapusa**, **Ponda**, and **Vasco**, with **Cycling** and **Golf** being the only events held in **New Delhi** due to infrastructure requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Performance and Awards:**

 
 
• **Maharashtra** finished at the top of the medal tally with a total of **228 medals** (80 gold, 69 silver, and 79 bronze), successfully claiming the **Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy**.
 
• The **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)** secured the second position with **66 gold medals**, while **Haryana** finished third with **62 gold medals**.
 
• **Srihari Nataraj**, a swimmer from **Karnataka**, was adjudged the **Best Male Athlete** for winning **8 gold**, **1 silver**, and **1 bronze** medal.
 
• **Sanyukta Prashen Kale** and **Pranati Nayak**, both gymnasts, were jointly named the **Best Female Athlete**.
 
 
 
• **Context and History:**
 
 
• The previous **36th National Games** were hosted by **Gujarat** in **2022** after a significant delay due to the pandemic.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of voluntary action seen in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Writing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Voluntary actions** are those activities in the human body that are performed under the **conscious control** and will of the individual. These actions are primarily regulated by the **cerebrum**, the largest part of the brain, which processes sensory information and initiates motor impulses.
 
• **Writing** is a classic example of a voluntary action as it involves **conscious thought**, decision-making, and memory. The **motor cortex** in the frontal lobe of the brain sends specific signals through the spinal cord to the skeletal muscles in the **fingers, hand, and wrist** to execute precise movements.
 
• Unlike reflexes, voluntary actions can be initiated, modified, or stopped at any moment based on **environmental stimuli** or personal choice. These actions are learned over time and require a high degree of **neuromuscular coordination** and cognitive processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Involuntary Actions:** These are spontaneous and automatic responses that do not require conscious thought. They are controlled by the **autonomous nervous system** and the **hindbrain**.

 
 
• **Vomiting:** This is a protective **reflex action** controlled by the **vomit center** located in the **medulla oblongata**. It is an involuntary ejection of stomach contents through the mouth.
 
• **Salivation:** This is an involuntary response to the sight, smell, or taste of food, managed by the **salivary nuclei** in the brainstem to facilitate **digestion**.
 
• **Breathing:** Although it can be modulated voluntarily for short durations, **respiration** is fundamentally an involuntary process driven by the **pons** and **medulla** to maintain **homeostasis** of oxygen and carbon dioxide levels.

questions.question: In Indian constitution, ______ may by law provide for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint with respect to the use, distribution or control of the waters of, or in, any inter-State River or river valley.

• The **Constitution** further provides under **Article 262(2)** that **Parliament** may, by law, exclude the jurisdiction of the **Supreme Court** or any other court in respect of such water disputes.
 
• This provision was included to ensure that complex **riparian issues** and **inter-state conflicts** are resolved through specialized mechanisms rather than standard judicial litigation, which might be time-consuming or technically limited.

• **River Boards Act, 1956**: This law provides for the establishment of **River Boards** for the regulation and development of **inter-State rivers**, aimed at advising the **Central Government** on coordination and development.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Distribution of Power**:
 
 
• **Entry 17** of the **State List** (List II) gives states power over water supplies, irrigation, and canals.
 
• **Entry 56** of the **Union List** (List I) gives the **Union** power over the regulation and development of **inter-State rivers** and river valleys to the extent declared by **Parliament** to be in the public interest.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a fire extinguisher?

options.text: To add more fuel to the fire
To increase the temperature of the fuel
To increase the supply of air
To cut off the supply of air, reduce the temperature of the fuel, or both

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To cut off the supply of air, reduce the temperature of the fuel, or both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fire is a chemical reaction known as **combustion**, which requires three fundamental components typically represented as the **Fire Triangle**: **Fuel** (combustible material), **Heat** (to reach ignition temperature), and **Oxygen** (usually from air).
 
• The fundamental principle of a **fire extinguisher** is to disrupt this **Fire Triangle** by removing or neutralizing one or more of its legs.
 
• Extinguishers like **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** work primarily by **displacing oxygen**. Since CO2 is heavier than air, it settles over the fire, creating a blanket that **cuts off the air supply** necessary for combustion.
 
• Water-based extinguishers function primarily by **absorbing heat** from the burning fuel, cooling it down below its **flash point** or **ignition temperature** to stop the reaction.
 
• Dry chemical extinguishers use agents like **Monoammonium Phosphate** to both smother the fire and interrupt the **chemical chain reaction** that sustains the flame.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fire extinguishers are categorized based on the types of fires they are designed to combat:
 
 
• **Class A**: Used for **ordinary solid combustibles** such as wood, paper, and textiles.
 
• **Class B**: Designed for **flammable liquids** like petrol, oil, and paint.
 
• **Class C**: Suitable for fires involving **flammable gases** like methane or propane.
 
• **Class D**: Specialized for **combustible metals** like magnesium or potassium.
 
• **Electrical Fires**: Often handled by non-conductive agents like **CO2** or **Halon** to prevent electrocution.
 
 
 
• The **PASS technique** is the standard operating procedure for using a portable fire extinguisher: **Pull** the pin, **Aim** at the base of the fire, **Squeeze** the trigger, and **Sweep** the nozzle from side to side.

questions.question: In the context of money supply in India, which of the following is NOT the Quantitative tool of Reserve bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moral suasion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** manages the **money supply** and **inflation** in the Indian economy through its **Monetary Policy**, which utilizes two types of instruments: **Quantitative** and **Qualitative**.
 
• **Quantitative tools** (General tools) are intended to regulate the total volume of **credit** and **liquidity** available in the banking system without discriminating between the sectors that receive the credit.
 
• **Qualitative tools** (Selective tools) are used to regulate the **direction** and **purpose** of credit flow toward specific sectors of the economy, such as agriculture or priority sectors.
 
• **Moral suasion** is a **Qualitative instrument** where the **RBI** uses persuasion, informal suggestions, or psychological pressure on **commercial banks** to align their lending activities with the central bank’s economic objectives.
 
• Unlike **Quantitative tools**, **Moral suasion** does not involve mandatory legal requirements or immediate changes in interest rates but relies on the **cooperation** of the banking community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quantitative Tools of RBI**:

 
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**: It is the percentage of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that commercial banks are legally required to maintain as **cash reserves** with the **RBI**.
 
• **Bank Rate**: This is the standard rate at which the **RBI** is prepared to buy or rediscount **bills of exchange** or other commercial papers, acting as a long-term interest rate signal for the economy.
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)**: This involves the simultaneous buying and selling of **Government Securities (G-Secs)** by the **RBI** to either inject liquidity into or absorb excess liquidity from the market.
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**: The minimum percentage of deposits that a bank must maintain in the form of **liquid assets** like gold or unencumbered government securities.
 
 
 
• **Other Qualitative Tools**:
 
 
• **Margin Requirements**: Adjusting the difference between the **market value** of a security and the **loan amount** granted against it.
 
• **Rationing of Credit**: Fixing a **ceiling** or maximum limit on credit for specific industries or sectors.

questions.question: Two numbers are such that their HCF is 18 and their LCM is 540. If the sum of the two numbers is 198, find the numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **divisibility** by **HCF (18)**: Only option (4) contains numbers where both 90 and 108 are multiples of 18.

Verify **Sum**: 90 + 108 = 198 (Matches the condition).

Verify **LCM**: Numbers are 18×5 and 18×6 ⇒ LCM = 18 × 5 × 6 = 540 (Matches the condition).

**∴ The correct answer is 90 and 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **HCF** = 18, **LCM** = 540, **Sum** = 198.

**Formula Used:** Product of numbers = HCF × LCM | Numbers can be assumed as **Ha** and **Hb** (where H is HCF and a, b are co-primes).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/933d007489b863c8a237a16c3090fe1ed7c2916b3a1f4ecc5e22962ffc551373.png] 

⇒ Let the numbers be 18a and 18b.

⇒ 18a + 18b = 198 ⇒ 18(a + b) = 198

⇒ a + b = 198 ÷ 18 = 11

⇒ LCM = 18 × a × b = 540

⇒ ab = 540 ÷ 18 = 30

⇒ We need two **co-prime numbers** whose sum is 11 and product is 30.

⇒ Solving x² − 11x + 30 = 0 ⇒ (x − 5)(x − 6) = 0

⇒ a = 5 and b = 6

⇒ Number 1 = 18 × 5 = 90

⇒ Number 2 = 18 × 6 = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 90 and 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Property

For any two numbers A and B, the relationship is: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

Co-prime Factorization

If H is the HCF of two numbers, the numbers can be written as H × x and H × y, where HCF(x, y) = 1.

LCM of Multiples

The LCM of two numbers Hx and Hy (where H is the HCF) is H × x × y.

questions.question: If sqrt{20.25}+sqrt{(16+x)}=9.5, then what is the value of x?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

First, calculate the **square root** of 20.25: √20.25 = 4.5.

Subtract 4.5 from the total sum: √(16 + x) = 9.5 − 4.5 = 5.

Square both sides to find the value inside the root: 16 + x = 5² = 25.

Solve for **x**: x = 25 − 16 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√20.25 + √(16 + x) = 9.5

**Calculation:**

⇒ √(2025/100) + √(16 + x) = 9.5

⇒ 45/10 + √(16 + x) = 9.5

⇒ 4.5 + √(16 + x) = 9.5

⇒ √(16 + x) = 9.5 − 4.5

⇒ √(16 + x) = 5

⇒ 16 + x = 5² (**Squaring both sides**)

⇒ 16 + x = 25

⇒ x = 25 − 16

⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimal Numbers

To find the square root of a decimal, convert it to a fraction with a power of 10 in the denominator, or calculate √N and adjust the decimal point (e.g., √20.25 = √2025 ÷ 10).

Squaring Rule

If √A = B, then A = B². This property is used to eliminate radical signs in algebraic equations.

Perfect Square Shortcut (Ending in 25)

The square root of a number ending in 25 always ends in 5. For 2025, since 4 × 5 = 20, the root is 45.

questions.question: The length of a rectangle is 5 cm. The diagonal of the rectangle is 13 cm. What is the ratio of length and breadth of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the standard **Pythagorean triplet**: 5, 12, 13.

In a **rectangle**, the **diagonal** acts as the hypotenuse (13 cm).

Since the given **length** is 5 cm, the **breadth** must be 12 cm.

Ratio of **length** to **breadth** = 5 : 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** (l) = 5 cm

**Diagonal** (d) = 13 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **rectangle**, d² = l² + b² (by **Pythagorean theorem**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12ef95f0d17bd3969bbe758edba427bf6b2d057e8cafb891ff8c62c0727345a0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 13² = 5² + b²

⇒ 169 = 25 + b²

⇒ b² = 169 − 25

⇒ b² = 144

⇒ b = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Ratio = Length : Breadth

⇒ Ratio = 5 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is given by Length × Breadth.

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total boundary length of the rectangle is 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

questions.question: The difference between the length and breadth of a rectangle is 8 metres. If its perimeter is 160 metres, then what will be the area (in square metre) of rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Semi-perimeter** (L + B) = 160 ÷ 2 = 80 m

Given difference (L − B) = 8 m

**Length (L)** = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (80 + 8) ÷ 2 = 44 m

**Breadth (B)** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (80 − 8) ÷ 2 = 36 m

**Area** = L × B = 44 × 36 = 1584 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1584 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of **rectangle** = 160 m

Difference between **length (L)** and **breadth (B)** = 8 m

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 2 × (L + B)

Area = L × B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c69b93312028916d7aa3fe06a00484072ef2bbcfde0fedf4d68228aa77a0482e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (L + B) = 160

⇒ L + B = 80 — (Eq. 1)

⇒ L − B = 8 — (Eq. 2)

Adding (Eq. 1) and (Eq. 2):

⇒ 2L = 88

⇒ L = 44 m

Subtracting (Eq. 2) from (Eq. 1):

⇒ 2B = 72

⇒ B = 36 m

Calculating the **Area**:

⇒ Area = 44 × 36

⇒ Area = 1584 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1584 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is given by d = √(L² + B²).

Square with Same Perimeter

For a fixed perimeter, the shape with the maximum area is a **square** where L = B.

Relation between L+B and L-B

(L + B)² − (L − B)² = 4 × L × B = 4 × Area.

questions.question: Average of 8 numbers is P. One number is removed. New average is P + 2. Which number was removed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a number is **removed** and the **average increases**, the removed number is always **less than** the original average.

**Total Increase** = Count of remaining numbers × Increase in average

Total Increase = 7 × 2 = 14

**Removed Number** = Original Average − Total Increase = P − 14

**∴ The correct answer is P − 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of **8 numbers** = **P**. After removing 1 number, the average of **7 numbers** = **P + 2**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of observations = Average × Total count of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ccfa61abafc29318188448bf227384a13fc223385a37de289cb1bfea75d47b1.png] 

⇒ Sum of original 8 numbers = 8 × P = 8P

⇒ Sum of remaining 7 numbers = 7 × (P + 2) = 7P + 14

⇒ Removed number = (Sum of 8 numbers) − (Sum of 7 numbers)

⇒ Removed number = 8P − (7P + 14)

⇒ Removed number = 8P − 7P − 14 = P − 14

**∴ The correct answer is P − 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Effect of Removal on Average

If the removed value is equal to the average, the average remains **unchanged**. If it is less than the average, the average **increases**.

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of **deviations** of all items from their arithmetic mean is always **zero**. This concept helps in solving complex average problems quickly.

questions.question: 23 consecutive natural numbers are given. These numbers are in ascending order. The average of last 11 numbers is 34. What is the average of all 23 numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **consecutive natural numbers**, the **average** is always the **middle term** of the series.

For 23 numbers, the middle term is the **12th number**.

The last 11 numbers are from the 13th to the 23rd position; their middle term is the **18th number**.

Given 18th number = 34 ⇒ 12th number = 18th number − (18 − 12) = 34 − 6 = 28.

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total numbers = 23; Numbers are **consecutive natural numbers** in **ascending order**; Average of last 11 numbers = 34.

**Formula:** Average of an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86f0ed6e58d1ab89b7a34722c59eaca2e239c936fa0cae5311cfce8ba3336429.png] 

Let the 23 consecutive numbers be x, x+1, x+2, ..., x+22.

⇒ The last 11 numbers are: (x+12), (x+13), ..., (x+22).

⇒ Average of last 11 = [(x + 12) + (x + 22)] ÷ 2

⇒ 34 = (2x + 34) ÷ 2

⇒ 34 = x + 17

⇒ x = 34 − 17 = 17

⇒ Average of all 23 numbers = [First term + Last term] ÷ 2

⇒ Average = [x + (x + 22)] ÷ 2 = x + 11

⇒ Average = 17 + 11 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any series in AP, the average is always the mean of the first and last terms: Average = (a + l) ÷ 2.

Middle Term Rule

If the number of terms (n) is odd, the average is the (n + 1)/2th term. If n is even, it is the mean of the two middle terms.

Sum of Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula S = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2.

questions.question: 40 men can build a wall in 50 days working 9 hours per day. How many men will be required to build the same wall in 75 days working 6 hours per day?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **MDH rule** for **proportionality**: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

Substitute: 40 × 50 × 9 = M₂ × 75 × 6

18000 = M₂ × 450

M₂ = 18000 ÷ 450 = 40 men

**∴ The correct answer is 40 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **40 men** can build a wall in **50 days** working **9 hours per day**. We need to find men required for **75 days** working **6 hours per day**.

**Formula Used:** Total Work (Man-Hours) = **Men × Days × Hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52c7f09bbb134b4101c882dbf08d62e1e4916cdafe986b22436b699a5063d40b.png] 

⇒ Total work in man-hours = 40 × 50 × 9 = 18,000 units

⇒ Total capacity needed in Case 2 = 75 days × 6 hours = 450 hours per man

⇒ Number of men (M₂) = Total work ÷ Total capacity per man

⇒ M₂ = 18,000 ÷ 450

⇒ M₂ = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

The general formula is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂) ÷ W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, E is efficiency, and W is work.

Inverse Variation

Number of men is **inversely proportional** to the number of days and hours required. If we increase the number of days or hours, fewer men are needed for the same work.

Unit of Work

When the **same wall** is mentioned, W₁ = W₂, which allows us to equate the products of men, days, and hours directly.

questions.question: Length of train A is 500 metres. Length of train B is 200 metres. Both the trains cross each other in 35 seconds. These trains are running in opposite direction. What is the total speed (in m/s) of A and B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **opposite direction**, relative speed is the **sum of speeds** of both trains.

**Relative Speed** = (Length of Train A + Length of Train B) ÷ Time

Total Speed = (500 + 200) ÷ 35

Total Speed = 700 ÷ 35 = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **Train A** (LA) = 500 m

Length of **Train B** (LB) = 200 m

**Time taken** to cross (T) = 35 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (in opposite direction) = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8eef31859b631b8e7af2f1371c0223202988d45da99cf9958a1e83da629b5ba.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = LA + LB

⇒ Total Distance = 500 + 200 = 700 m

⇒ Total Speed (VA + VB) = Total Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Total Speed = 700 ÷ 35

⇒ Total Speed = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = |V₁ − V₂|.

Unit Conversion (km/h to m/s)

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. For example, 72 km/h = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole or man, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train itself.

questions.question: The speed of a train is 10 km/hr. Length of the train is 250 metres. How much time (in minutes) the train will take to cross a man standing on the platform?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Speed** to **metres per minute**: 10 km/hr = (10 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 500/3 m/min.

**Time** taken to cross a **stationary man** = **Length of Train** ÷ **Speed**.

Time = 250 ÷ (500/3) = 250 × 3 ÷ 500 = 3/2 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Length of train** (L) = 250 m

**Formula:**

**Time** = **Distance** ÷ **Speed**

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed** in m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 50/18 = 25/9 m/s

⇒ **Time** (in sec) = 250 ÷ (25/9)

⇒ **Time** = 250 × 9 ÷ 25

⇒ **Time** = 10 × 9 = 90 seconds

⇒ **Time** (in min) = 90 ÷ 60

⇒ **Time** = 3/2 minutes

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a **point object** (man, pole, tree), the distance covered equals the **length of the train**.

Crossing Lengthy Objects

When a train crosses a **platform** or **bridge**, the distance covered equals (Length of Train + Length of Platform).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the **same direction**, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. If in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

• **Modals**: For simple modals like **can, may, must, should**, the passive form is **modal + be + V3**. For modal perfects like **must have, could have, should have**, the form is **modal + have + been + V3**.
 
• **Agent Omission**: We omit the **prepositional phrase** beginning with **'by'** when the doer is **unimportant**, **unknown**, or **obvious** from the context (e.g., 'The thief was arrested' implies the police did it).
 
• **Tense Consistency**: The **Passive Voice** must always maintain the **aspect** and **tense** of the original active sentence.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Incorrect Forms**:
 
 
• **Grammatical Errors**: Using **'call'** instead of the **past participle 'called'** violates the basic rule of passive construction.
 
• **Structural Errors**: Omitting the auxiliary **'been'** results in an active verb form, which fails to convey that the action was performed upon the subject.
 
• **Modal Misuse**: Adding unnecessary words like **'to be'** after **'have'** changes the grammatical necessity and creates a non-standard English structure.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
They will distribute sweets among the poor.

options.text: Sweets are to be distributed by them among the poor.
Sweets will be distribute among the poor by them.
Sweets will be distributed among the poor by them.
Sweets will distributed among the poor by them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sweets will be distributed among the poor by them.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence 'They will distribute sweets among the poor' is in the **Active Voice** and follows the **Simple Future Tense** (also known as Future Indefinite).
 
• In **Simple Future Tense**, the active structure is **Subject + will/shall + Base Verb (V1) + Object**.
 
• When converting to **Passive Voice**, the structure transforms to **Object + will/shall + be + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• The **Object** of the active sentence (**sweets**) becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence.
 
• The **Subject** of the active sentence (**They**) changes to its **Objective Case** (**them**) and is placed after the preposition **by**.
 
• The verb **distribute** is replaced by **will be distributed** to satisfy the requirement of the **Future Passive** form.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Future Passive Rules:**
 
 
• **Auxiliary Verb:** In the passive voice for future tense, the modal **will** or **shall** must always be followed by **be**.
 
• **Main Verb:** The main action must always be expressed in the **Third Form of the Verb (V3)**, which is **distributed** in this instance.
 
• **Contextual Placement:** Adverbial phrases or complements like **among the poor** are typically placed after the main verb to maintain the flow of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Case Shifts:**
 
 
• Personal pronouns undergo a change from **Nominative Case** to **Objective Case**. For example, **I** becomes **me**, **He** becomes **him**, and **They** becomes **them**.
 
 
 
• **Function of Passive Voice:**
 
 
• The **Passive Voice** is utilized when the focus is intended to be on the **recipient** of the action (the sweets) rather than the **doer** (them).
 
 
</ul

Regular exercise __will have the effect of increasing your energy levels__ and help you feel more refreshed throughout the day.

will affect the increase of your energy levels

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**will increase your energy levels**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The underlined phrase **'will have the effect of increasing'** is an example of **circumlocution**, which refers to the use of unnecessarily many words to describe a simple action. Replacing it with the single, direct verb **'will increase'** significantly improves the sentence's **conciseness** and **readability**.

• The sentence requires **parallel structure** to maintain grammatical balance between the two predicates joined by the coordinating conjunction **'and'**. By using the future tense verb **'will increase'**, the first part of the sentence becomes parallel with the second part, **'and help you feel'**.

• Using **strong action verbs** instead of **nominalized phrases** (turning a verb into a noun phrase like 'have the effect of') makes the prose more **direct** and **impactful**. In **standard English grammar**, avoiding excessive **wordiness** is a key principle for sentence improvement.

• The original phrasing is **wordy** and creates a **clunky flow**. Modern **style guides** (such as **The Chicago Manual of Style** or **Strunk and White**) recommend opting for the most economical expression that preserves the original meaning.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Linguistic and Stylistic Concepts**:

• **Affect vs. Effect**: These are **homophones** often confused in competitive exams. **'Affect'** is typically used as a **verb** meaning to influence or change (e.g., The weather **affects** energy levels), while **'Effect'** is typically used as a **noun** meaning a result (e.g., The **effect** of exercise is positive). Option 2 is incorrect as it uses **'affect'** where a noun is needed, and Option 3 uses it awkwardly.

• **Parallelism**: This is a **rhetorical device** where parts of a sentence are grammatically similar or identical in structure, sound, or meaning. Correcting the sentence to **'Regular exercise will [increase] ... and [help] ...'** follows this rule of **structural consistency**.

• **Economy of Language**: This refers to the practice of using the **minimum number of words** necessary to convey a message without losing clarity. It is a highly valued trait in **standardized English proficiency tests**.

</ul
